newsitem.title: CHINA: China attributes falling prices to ample supply.
newsitem.headline: China attributes falling prices to ample supply.

text.p: Two successive record grain harvests and an ample supply of industrial products were major factors in China's success in curbing inflation in 1996, Ye Zhen, spokesman of the State Statistical Bureau said on Monday.

"It was mainly because of rising supply caused by two consecutive record grain harvests and sufficient supply of most industrial products," Ye told a news conference. China's retail price inflation was estimated at 6.0 percent for the whole of 1996, down from 14.8 percent in 1995 and compared with a communist-era high of 21.4 percent in 1994.
Consumer price inflation was estimated at 8.3 percent for 1996, he said. That was down from 17.1 percent last year.
The 6.0 percent figure for 1996 retail price inflation, China's benchmark price index, was well below the government's 10 percent target for the year.
The bureau estimated a record grain harvest of 480 million tonnes for 1996, up from a previous record of 466 million tonnes last year.
The record harvests have depressed domestic prices of corn this year while supply of rice has also exceeded demand, official media have reported.
Output of most industrial products had outstripped market demand, and while this had cooled inflation it had resulted in rising stockpiles, Ye said.

Inventories among 380,000 industrial firms were valued at 540 billion yuan at the end of October, up by 80 billion yuan from the start of 1996, he said. Of the total, 150 billion yuan were stockpiles of goods that could not be sold.
Tight monetary policy, a policy now well into its fourth year, had kept a lid on strong demand for consumer goods and further dampened inflation, he said.
Administrative measures by regional government officials, who have been made personally responsible for holding down prices, had helped to tame inflation, Ye said.
"Since we managed to keep inflation at a relatively low level, and below the rate of economic growth, we can say that this was a success," he said.
